metadata.note: The Reading and Columbia Railroad (Sinking Spring - Columbia, PA, 1864; Lancaster Branch 1866), its operation by the Philadelphia & Reading / Reading Company, the leased Lancaster - Quarryville line (1875-1895) and the Marietta Branch (1884 anchor). One feature per drawable span x operator; the R&C / Reading Rule 4 split at 1870 shares identical geometry (the Reading's Sinking Spring - Lancaster feature is the R&C main line north of Lancaster Junction plus the Lancaster Branch, vertex for vertex). Research report: research/branches/reading_and_columbia_railroad.txt (researched 2026-10-22). Trains reached Reading over the P&R Lebanon Valley line from Sinking Spring (5.7 mi), which is not drawn in this layer or anywhere else in the dataset yet.
sources: research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt (Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952)

metadata.operator_split: Split ONCE, at 1870: Reading and Columbia Railroad 1864-1870 (own colour #3B8C7A), Philadelphia & Reading / Reading Company from 1870 (colour pulled programmatically from reading_main_line.geojson). The 1896 and 1923-24 Reading reorganisations and the 31 Dec 1945 merger of the R&C into the Reading Company are corporate changes only and do not split. The 1870 change of operator rests on one UNCITED Wikipedia sentence ('The Reading leased it in 1870'); the Columbia Historic Preservation Society instead says the Reading Company 'assumed the operation' of the R&C after the 1923 consolidation. Source conflict, recorded per Rule 3; 1870 is used because it is the only date any source gives for the P&R taking the road over.
not_yet_sourced: P&R takeover date: 1870 (Wikipedia 'Reading Company', uncited) vs 'after the 1923 merger' (Columbia Historic Preservation Society). If CHS is right, the R&C-coloured features should run to 1924 and the Reading ones start then. Settle with the P&R annual report 1870-71, Poor's Manual, or John D. Denney Jr., 'The Reading and Columbia Railroad', Journal of the Lancaster County Historical Society (1963).

OPEN end - Philadelphia and Reading: Lancaster Junction - Columbia is drawn to 1884, the last confirmed passenger year, not a known end. A dated Reading timetable or a Columbia 'last train' story is needed to extend it (possibly to 1950).

ANCHOR + OPEN - Philadelphia and Reading: Marietta Branch is drawn for 1884 only; who ran its trains (P&R/R&C or the Reading, Marietta & Hanover), whether they reached Marietta proper, and when passengers ended are all unknown.
Lancaster Branch end: 5 Nov 1950 is RP's date for 'the Reading & Columbia Branch'; that it covers Lancaster is inferred from the 1951 table title READING AND LANCASTER (medium confidence).
Quarryville lease end: 1895 (W2K) vs 1900 (FROIO); drawn to 1895. The post-Reading PRR-interest operation (to c.1909) belongs to PRR research and is not drawn.
First passenger train: 26 Dec 1863 at Lititz per a Lititz Record Express article known only from a search extract; drawn from 1864.
Headways and speeds throughout are estimates; no running time or frequency was found for any year except AR/RP's 'up to ten passenger trains a day'.
omitted: Report block [6], Reading excursions over the R&C after Nov 1950 'through the early 1960s' (RP): drawable NONE - no dated trip.

Report block [7], Mount Hope Branch (Manheim - Mount Hope): drawable NONE as an R&C/Reading feature; the only dated passenger trains are Cornwall Railroad through trains, handled in cornwall_and_lebanon_railroad.geojson.
Modern freight-only operators of R&C remnants (NS Lititz Industrial Track, Columbia & Reading Railway, Landisville Railroad, East Penn's Lancaster Northern): Rule 1, used for geometry only.

segments.note: Reading and Columbia Railroad, Sinking Spring (junction with the Philadelphia & Reading's Lebanon Valley line, over which trains ran the last 5.7 mi into Reading - not drawn here) - Fritztown - Reinholds - Denver - Ephrata - Akron - Rothsville - Lititz - Manheim - Lancaster Junction - Landisville - Marietta Junction - Hempfield - Ironville - Columbia. Columbia - Manheim was completed by 1 Jan 1862 (CHS) but no passenger train on it is dated before the line opened through: CHS gives the first regular passenger schedule Columbia - Reading as 1 April 1864, BERKS says the first passenger train ran through from Reading to Columbia in May 1864, and an officials' special ran 15 March 1864 (LCM) - sources disagree on the month, not the year. A Lititz Record Express article (known only from a search-engine extract, not read) dates the first passenger train at Lititz to 26 Dec 1863; not drawn. Steam from opening; no animal traction. Ends 1870 because the operator changes, not service: The 1870 change of operator rests on one UNCITED Wikipedia sentence ('The Reading leased it in 1870'); the Columbia Historic Preservation Society instead says the Reading Company 'assumed the operation' of the R&C after the 1923 consolidation. Source conflict, recorded per Rule 3; 1870 is used because it is the only date any source gives for the P&R taking the road over. Service continues as the Philadelphia and Reading features. headway_min 180 is an ESTIMATE; no frequency was found for these years.
sources: Segment-level: start year from CHS (1 Apr 1864 schedule), BERKS (May 1864 through train) and LCM (15 Mar 1864 special); end year is the operator change dated only by WPRDG (uncited) and contradicted by CHS - see note. Headway not sourced.

segments.note: The Reading and Columbia as the Philadelphia & Reading's (from 1896/1924 the Reading Company's) 'Reading & Columbia Branch': Reading - Sinking Spring - Ephrata - Lititz - Manheim - Lancaster Junction - Lancaster (Prince St; brick passenger station 1907-1967, W2K). Starts 1870 at the change of operator - The 1870 change of operator rests on one UNCITED Wikipedia sentence ('The Reading leased it in 1870'); the Columbia Historic Preservation Society instead says the Reading Company 'assumed the operation' of the R&C after the 1923 consolidation. Source conflict, recorded per Rule 3; 1870 is used because it is the only date any source gives for the P&R taking the road over. The R&C company kept separate accounts (BERKS reports its own traffic: 248,335 passengers in 1876, 233,044 in 1880, 346,600 in 1884) and was merged into the Reading Company on 31 Dec 1945, a corporate change only. Up to ten passenger trains a day in the heyday (AR, RP); Reading Ramble excursion 4 Oct 1936; motor cars at the end. Ends 5 Nov 1950: 'Regular passenger service on the Reading & Columbia Branch, which included use of motor cars, ended on November 5, 1950' (RP); the Feb 1952 Official Guide daggers Lititz, Manheim and Millway 'for freight only' and prints 'Freight Service' over its READING AND LANCASTER table. That the 1950 date covers the Lancaster Branch specifically is inferred from that table's title (medium confidence). Several Reading excursions ran over the branch after Nov 1950 'through the early 1960s' (RP) but none is dated, so none is drawn. Freight continued (steam to 1956, Conrail 1976); Ephrata - Lititz abandoned 1985 and is now the Warwick to Ephrata Rail Trail; Lititz - Lancaster is NS's Lititz Industrial Track. headway_min 180 is an ESTIMATE from 'up to ten trains a day'.
sources: Segment-level: end date 5 Nov 1950 from RP, corroborated by the Feb 1952 Official Guide index daggers (Lititz 306972, Manheim 310160, Millway 313786) and Table 10 'Freight Service'; Fowler RDG section 168 confirms passenger stations in the 1875 and 1884 Official Guides. Start year is the contested operator change (WPRDG vs CHS). Headway estimated from AR/RP 'up to ten trains a day'.

segments.note: Philadelphia & Reading operation of the R&C's original southern leg, Lancaster Junction - Landisville - Marietta Junction - Hempfield - Ironville - Columbia. Starts 1870 at the change of operator - The 1870 change of operator rests on one UNCITED Wikipedia sentence ('The Reading leased it in 1870'); the Columbia Historic Preservation Society instead says the Reading Company 'assumed the operation' of the R&C after the 1923 consolidation. Source conflict, recorded per Rule 3; 1870 is used because it is the only date any source gives for the P&R taking the road over. OPEN END: 1884 is the last CONFIRMED passenger year on this leg (Fowler's 1884 Official Guide letter at Marietta Junction, and BERKS's 1884 passenger count for the whole road), NOT a known end. Service almost certainly ran later - possibly to 1950 - but no source found dates a passenger train in Columbia after 1884: the Feb 1952 Guide daggers Hempfield freight-only (only 'before 1951'), and the 1951 Reading table is titled READING AND LANCASTER. Do not extend without evidence. Columbia station shed torn down 1941, station 1966 (W2K). Today the Columbia & Reading Railway and Landisville Railroad (both freight) work surviving pieces. headway_min 240 is an ESTIMATE.
sources: Segment-level: Fowler RDG section 168 (1875 Guide at Landisville, Ironville, Bruckarts, Columbia; 1884 Guide at Marietta Junction) and BERKS (1884 traffic) for the last confirmed year; start is the contested operator change (WPRDG vs CHS). Headway not sourced.

segments.note: Lancaster (King St) - Conestoga Furnace - Levan's Mills - West Willow - Pequea - Refton - New Providence - Hess - Quarryville. Built (standard gauge, despite its name) by the Lancaster and Reading Narrow Gauge Railroad and opened May 1875 (BERKS 'extended to Quarryville, fifteen miles, in May, 1875'; Fowler 1875 Guide at West Willow, New Providence, Cabeen's, Quarryville), and leased to and run by the Reading / R&C as an extension of its Lancaster Branch (FROIO); Fowler's 1893 timetable letter confirms trains under the lease. End: W2K says the Reading 'gave up its lease on the line in 1895'; FROIO has the lease voided on mortgage default and the property auctioned to PRR interests in 1900 - the bracket 1895-1900 is collapsed to the earlier date. Afterwards the L&RNG / Lancaster & Quarryville under PRR interests (merged into the PRR 30 Apr 1915), passenger service to about 1909 (W2K, AR-Q) - a different company, not drawn here; the 1896-1899 operator is unknown. Abandoned after Hurricane Agnes, June 1972. headway_min 360 is an ESTIMATE.
sources: Segment-level: start from BERKS (May 1875) and Fowler PRR section 21 (1875 Guide); 1893 operation from Fowler (1893t); end 1895 from W2K, with FROIO's 1900 recorded as a conflict. Headway not sourced.

segments.note: Marietta Junction - Farmdale - Copenheffer - Florinel - Chickies (PRR). Built as the Reading, Marietta & Hanover RR, a P&R-allied company (Fowler's heading), opened August 1883 (BERKS 'Chiques to Marietta (six miles)'); part of the P&R's plan to reach Hanover across the Susquehanna, which was never bridged. ANCHOR: 1884 is the ONE proven passenger year - Fowler's 1884 Official Guide letter at Marietta Junction and Chickies. Service certainly ran wider both ways (the line opened in 1883) but no other year is confirmed; the end is unknown (OPEN). Do not widen without evidence. OPERATOR NOT ESTABLISHED: drawn in the Philadelphia and Reading colour because BERKS counts it among the R&C's branches and the R&C was P&R-operated from 1870 on this dataset's reading; it may instead have been worked by the RM&H itself. Whether trains ran on into Marietta over the PRR is not established. headway_min 480 is an ESTIMATE.
sources: Segment-level: 1884 from Fowler RDG section 170 (1884 Official Guide letter at Marietta Junction and Chickies); opening Aug 1883 from BERKS. Operator and headway not sourced.
